transport.modes.Walking.miles_pp.note: NTS0303c, England only, used as a UK proxy as in the 2018 baseline.

transport.modes.Cycling.miles_pp.note: NTS0303c, England only, used as a UK proxy as in the 2018 baseline.

transport.modes.Ebikes.miles_pp.note: Not separated in NTS or TSGB. Zero as in the 2018 baseline.

transport.modes.Rail.miles_pp.note: 2018 baseline 754 miles per person, scaled by TSGB0101 rail passenger km {year} over 2018 (both from the current edition, which absorbs DfT revisions) and by 2018 population (66460000, the 2018 baseline value) over {year} population.

transport.modes.Rail.prc.EV.note: Share of rail passenger km on electric traction, calibrated so modelled rail electricity equals DUKES 1.1 rail electricity. Uses the ZCB electric efficiency (0.9) and mechanical kWh per passenger km. Diesel efficiency is calibrated separately to DUKES rail petroleum.

transport.modes.Bus.miles_pp.note: 2018 baseline 325 miles per person, scaled by TSGB0101 buses and coaches passenger km {year} over 2018 (both from the current edition, which absorbs DfT revisions) and by 2018 population (66460000, the 2018 baseline value) over {year} population.

transport.modes.Bus.prc.EV.note: Battery electric share of licensed buses and coaches at the end of {year} (VEH1103, UK), used as the share of bus miles.

transport.modes.Bus.prc.H2.note: Fuel cell buses are about 0.06% of the fleet. Negligible.

transport.modes.Motorbike.miles_pp.note: 2018 baseline 46 miles per person, scaled by TSGB0101 motorcycles passenger km {year} over 2018 (both from the current edition, which absorbs DfT revisions) and by 2018 population (66460000, the 2018 baseline value) over {year} population.

transport.modes.Motorbike.prc.EV.note: Battery electric share of licensed motorcycles at the end of {year} (VEH1103, UK), used as the share of miles.

motorcycles.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

diesel.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

petrol.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

transport.modes.Motorbike.efficiency.IC.note: Calibrated so modelled motorcycle fuel equals DUKES 1.1 road liquid fuel times the C8 motorcycle share.

transport.modes.Cars & Vans.miles_pp.note: 2018 baseline 6299 miles per person, scaled by TSGB0101 cars, vans and taxis passenger km {year} over 2018 (both from the current edition, which absorbs DfT revisions) and by 2018 population (66460000, the 2018 baseline value) over {year} population.

transport.modes.Cars & Vans.load_factor.note: Carried from the 2018 workbook (1.64 occupants of 5 seats).

_transport.car_bev_stock_share.note: Evidence for the car EV share. Battery electric share of licensed cars at the end of {year} (VEH1103, UK).

transport.modes.Cars & Vans.prc.EV.note: Share of car miles. Battery electric cars were 3.8% of the licensed stock at the end of 2024 (see _transport.car_bev_stock_share), and newer cars are driven further than the fleet average, so 5% is used.

transport.modes.Cars & Vans.prc.H2.note: Fuel cell cars are about 100 vehicles. Negligible.

_transport.road_liquid_ktoe.note: DUKES 1.1 road transport petroleum products plus bioenergy for 2024. Excludes natural gas and electricity. The sheet name is fixed at 2024.

cars.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

diesel.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

petrol.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

_transport.c8_cars_share.note: Share of C8 road petrol and diesel used by cars. ECUK C8 runs a year behind, so the 2023 row is used for a 2024 baseline.

_transport.car_fuel_TWh.note: Car liquid fuel including biofuel: DUKES road liquid fuel allocated by the C8 car share. 1 ktoe = 0.01163 TWh.

transport.modes.Cars & Vans.efficiency.I.note: Engine efficiency divisor calibrated so modelled car IC fuel equals _transport.car_fuel_TWh. Fuel is inversely proportional to it.

transport.modes.Aviation.miles_pp.note: 2018 baseline 3580 miles per person, scaled by AVI0201c passenger km flown by UK registered airlines (all services) {year} over 2018 and by 2018 population (66460000) over {year} population.

_transport.bev_cars_thousands.note: Battery electric cars licensed at the end of the year (VEH1103, UK).

transport.electric_car_battery_capacity.note: Battery electric cars times 60 kWh, an assumed fleet average battery. Only buffers the standard charging profile while smart charging and V2G are off.

transport.electric_car_max_charge_rate.note: Battery electric cars times 7 kW, an assumed typical home charger. The model scales it by the share of cars plugged in each hour.

transport.rail_freight_elec_demand.note: Rail freight is not separated, as in the 2018 baseline.

transport.freight_BEV_demand.note: Battery electric LGVs and HGVs are under 2% of the fleet. Their electricity is in the DUKES road electricity row, which this baseline does not allocate.

hgv.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

lgv.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

diesel.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

petrol.block: Road transport energy use by vehicle type

_transport.c8_freight_share.note: Share of C8 road petrol and diesel used by HGVs and LGVs, 2023 row.

transport.freight_IC_demand.note: HGV and LGV liquid fuel including biofuel (DUKES road liquid fuel allocated by the C8 freight share) plus DUKES national navigation. Allocating the DUKES total by C8 shares replaces the 2018 workbook's separate 'other road' balancing item.

transport.modes.Bus.efficiency.IC.note: Calibrated so modelled bus fuel equals DUKES 1.1 road liquid fuel times the C8 bus share, as for cars and freight.

transport.modes.Rail.efficiency.IC.note: Calibrated so modelled diesel rail fuel equals DUKES 1.1 rail petroleum. The electric share stays a judgement value.

transport.modes.Aviation.efficiency.IC.note: Calibrated so modelled aviation fuel equals DUKES 1.1 air (domestic and international). Passenger km are UK airlines only, so this also absorbs that boundary difference.

synth_fuel.biofuel_supply_TWhy.note: Transport biofuel (road and aviation) from DUKES 1.1. The model supplies it to the liquid fuel store, so fossil oil falls by the same amount.
